topic: Shapes of s, p and d Orbitals
title: Why Is p a Dumbbell? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A fast fan looks like a blurred disc, a bee keeps buzzing around one flower, and a swing in a night photo becomes a smear. We cannot follow the thing itself, only where it is likely to be. Electrons are the same. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we see the real shapes of s, p and d orbitals.

You will see how a dot picture of probability density (psi squared) becomes a boundary surface diagram that holds about 90 percent of the chance. On the molecule bench, drawn as flat cross-sections: 1s, 2s and 3s spheres with their radial nodes, the dumbbell-shaped p orbitals with a nodal plane (px, py and pz, same energy, different direction), and the five d orbitals (dxy, dyz, dzx, dx2-y2 and dz2, all five 3d with the same energy). We compare the nodes of 2s and 2p, derive the node rules step by step (angular nodes = l, radial nodes = n - l - 1, total = n - 1), count the nodes of 3d and 4p, and finish with the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 23 of our PUC Chemistry series. Episode 22 covers orbitals and quantum numbers.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
